text:
RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 35

An all-male panel is context, not evidence. Panels mirror who holds senior banking roles; four men on a risk committee is unremarkable and proves nothing on its own. Lead with it and you look like you're arguing from demographics rather than merit.

Your stronger facts are substantive: a PhD and nine years in the specific discipline versus a master's and a vaguely worded "broad experience of regulatory affairs," plus two weeks of silence on a reasonable request. In many jurisdictions, unexplained appointment of an apparently less-qualified candidate can shift the burden onto the employer.

So: chase the written reasons formally, in writing, with a deadline. Compare qualifications point by point. Mention composition once, as background.

Note: a head-of-function role may genuinely prioritise regulator-facing skill over modelling depth — that's a legitimate reason, and their answer will tell you which this was.
